sources: SATURDAY Oct 24 2026 RUN (markets closed). All market tiles are FRIDAY Oct 23 US closes - this is the first run of the week that captures a full completed session rather than a pre-open snapshot. THE OCT 22 GROWTH SCARE DID NOT REVERSE ON FRIDAY, IT BROADENED. HEADLINE 1 - CREDIT WIDENED AND THE STALE TILE FLAGGED LAST RUN RESOLVED TO THE BAD SIDE. FRED BAMLH0A0HYM2 has now posted Oct 22 at 3.40 pct, UP 13bp from 3.27 Oct 21 (3.33 Oct 20, 3.29 Oct 19, 3.31 Oct 16, 3.23 Oct 15). HY OAS is 340bp, the widest of the month and about 28bp above the 312 band that held through early October. Last run explicitly warned that 327 was a floor rather than a reading because FRED had not yet posted the risk-off session; that warning was correct. Credit is now confirming the equity and rate-vol stress instead of contradicting it, which removes the main reassuring counterweight on this board. Trend up. HEADLINE 2 - BRENT BROKE 116 ON AN ATTACK ON TANKERS, STILL WITH NO BARREL CONFIRMED LOST. Brent closed Oct 23 at 116.72 USD/Bbl, PLUS 3.14 pct and a sixth consecutive run above 110, with WTI at 103.27. TradingEconomics shows 116.72-116.91 at the Saturday snapshot. The driver: Iran's Revolutionary Guard said it struck four tankers transferring oil in the northern Gulf and that three more vessels hit mines west of Hormuz, with Iranian state TV claiming seven tankers burned or damaged. THE ASSOCIATED PRESS COULD NOT VERIFY THE CLAIM and President Trump called it invented, saying Iran is trying to lift oil prices before the US midterms. Separately Aramco has told Dhahran HQ staff to work remotely, drones were intercepted over Riyadh and Medina, and an attack on Dammam airport killed two and injured eight. CRITICAL QUALIFIER, SIXTH RUN: no Saudi barrels have been lost. Aramco's CEO says the East-West pipeline, which bypasses Hormuz, has been raised from 2 to 7 million b/d, its maximum, after flows were halted Oct 5 by a Houthi strike on a pumping station. So 116 is still risk premium plus an unverified claim, not a barrel-count problem - but the premium is now being paid on shipping risk inside the Gulf itself, which is a harder thing to arbitrage away than a Red Sea reroute. Trend up. HEADLINE 3 - EQUITIES FELL AGAIN AND THE LEADERSHIP INVERTED. S and P 500 7,623 minus 0.52 pct, Nasdaq Composite 25,955 minus 0.21 pct, Dow 52,214 MINUS 1.24 pct, minus 653 points. Note the reversal from Thursday: on Oct 22 the Dow held flat while the Nasdaq lost 2.6 pct; on Oct 23 the Dow was the worst index and the Nasdaq the most resilient. Two consecutive down sessions with rotating leadership is broad de-risking rather than a single-sector repricing. VIX closed 19.45, plus 2.21 pct, a second consecutive rise (19.03 Oct 22, 16.68 Oct 21) but still BELOW the 19.99 of Oct 16, so week-on-week equity vol is flat, not escalating. Trend flat. RATE VOL - PARTIAL RETRACEMENT, WHICH IS THE WEEK'S ONE CLEAN POSITIVE. MOVE 103.31 Oct 23, MINUS 3.30 pct from the 106.84 month-high of Oct 22 (95.94 Oct 21, 101.70 Oct 20, 101.30 Oct 19, 101.10 Oct 16). Rate vol gave back about a third of Thursday's 11 pct spike and sits only 2.2 pct above its level a week ago. The macro-stress signal that fired on Oct 22 did not extend. Trend flat. RATES - THE DURATION RALLY HELD. 10Y 4.987 pct and 2Y 4.68 pct at Friday's close, so the 10Y gave back only about 3bp of Thursday's 17-19bp collapse and the curve is 0.31 - unchanged on the day, DOWN 4bp from 0.35 a week ago. FRED T10Y2Y has not yet posted Oct 23; its last print is Oct 22 at 0.31, identical to the close-derived figure, so this tile is solid. A 10Y that stays below 5.00 pct while Brent gains another 3 pct is the bond market repeating Thursday's message rather than retracting it. Trend down. BREAKEVENS - THE KEY WATCH ITEM IS STILL UNRESOLVED. FRED T5YIFR remains 2.19 pct for Oct 22 (2.34 Oct 21, 2.31 Oct 20, 2.32 Oct 19, 2.33 Oct 16); the Oct 23 print has NOT been posted at run time. The single most important pending number on this board is therefore still pending: whether the violent 15bp break below the 2.31-2.34 band holds or snaps back. Carried at 2.19, trend down. DOLLAR - WILL NOT BID, SEVENTH RUN. DXY 101.72 Oct 23, plus 0.11 pct (101.65 Oct 22). EUR/USD 1.1193. The dollar is now flat to marginally higher on the week and has declined to rally through a sixth consecutive Brent print above 110, an attack on Gulf tanker traffic, two down equity sessions, a 13bp credit widening and a 15bp breakeven collapse. This remains the most persistent anomaly on the board. Trend flat. GROWTH PROXY - UP, AND THIS TIME FOR A SLIGHTLY BETTER REASON. Copper-gold 1.62 (copper 6.47 USD/Lbs PLUS 1.62 pct, gold 3,993.96 USD/t.oz minus 0.77 pct; 6.47/3993.96*1000 = 1.620). Last run the ratio rose almost entirely because gold was being liquidated; on Friday copper did most of the work, rising 1.6 pct while gold's decline slowed to under 1 pct. Gold has now broken BELOW 4,000 for the first time in over two months and is down seven straight sessions from 4,181, which through a Gulf escalation remains the second-strangest reading here after the dollar. Trend up. CONSUMER SENTIMENT - NEW PRINT AND A CORRECTION TO THIS BOARD. The UMich October FINAL released Oct 23 at 48.0, versus 48.1 in September - essentially unchanged month-on-month and still a five-month low. THIS IS A CORRECTION: the board was carrying 46.3 as the October preliminary, which was inconsistent with the published index level. FRED UMCSENT confirms Sep 2026 at 48.1 (51.7 Aug, 55.2 Jul, 49.5 Jun, 44.8 May) and sca.isr.umich.edu confirms the October final at 48.0. The tile is therefore reset to 48.0 and the trend to flat. The level is still historically dismal - roughly where sentiment sat at the 2022 inflation trough - and press coverage frames it as cost-of-living frustration heading into the midterms, but the month-on-month deterioration the board implied was not real. LABOUR - CARRIED, STILL THE STRONGEST TILE. FRED ICSA confirms 194k for the week ending Oct 17, the lowest in three months, down from 200k Oct 10 (198k Oct 3, 199k Sep 26, 198k Sep 19). Next release Oct 29. Note again that continuing claims rose 25k to 1.73 million, a six-week high: very little firing, visibly less hiring. Trend down, which is good. REAL ECONOMY - ALL OTHER TILES CARRIED, NO RELEASES: building permits 1,400k SAAR (September, next mid-November); ISM Manufacturing 54.5 (September, next Nov 2); Sahm Rule 0.00 (September, next Nov 6, trigger plus 0.50); LEI y/y plus 1.2 pct (September, released Oct 22, index unchanged at 99.6 with six-month growth plus 0.6 pct; no new release so trend reset from up to flat). FINANCIAL CONDITIONS - CARRIED, AND THE NEXT READ IS THE WEEK'S BIG ONE. FRED NFCI is still minus 0.496 for the week ending Oct 16 (minus 0.502 Oct 9, minus 0.508 Oct 2, minus 0.518 Sep 25). The Oct 28 release will be the first to contain both Oct 22 and Oct 23 and is the most important scheduled number on this board. Trend flat. MONETARY PLUMBING - STILL BLIND, NINTH RUN. The 3M SOFR-OIS spread was searched again; every free source serves the SOFR level or an OIS rate but never the spread, so 0bp is CARRIED AS A STANDING ASSUMPTION, NOT A MEASUREMENT. The EUR/USD 3M cross-currency basis is likewise CARRIED AS AN ASSUMPTION at minus 10bp. Global liquidity 1 (stable), carried: the Fed H.4.1 for Oct 21 showed total assets 6,753,604 million USD, minus 2,035 million on the week and plus 2.5 pct on the year, with no regime change found for the ECB, PBOC or BOJ; the next H.4.1 is Oct 29. Two assumed tiles and one judgement tile out of eighteen, unchanged for a ninth run. FED: the Oct 27-28 FOMC is NEXT WEEK, target 3.75-4.00 pct. A hold remains the heavy consensus and markets have priced out any hike; after Thursday's yield collapse and Friday's credit widening the risk is clearly a dovish surprise rather than a hawkish one. INFRASTRUCTURE: git healthy before this run (HEAD at a36a8ab, Oct 22 commit), this scheduled session remains the sole writer of data.json, the GitHub Action stays disabled since Oct 17, BDTI stays removed. NOTE: .git still holds roughly 150 renamed lock files (HEAD.lock.dead.*, index.lock.stale.* and similar) accumulated because this session cannot delete files in the folder - harmless but should be cleared. STILL OPEN - SECURITY, NINTH RUN: the origin remote is an HTTPS URL with a GitHub personal access token in plain text in .git/config. Fine-grained and repo-scoped, but it should be rotated and replaced with an SSH remote. Also still present: untracked junk in the repo root - _stale_git_locks/, _wtest, __pycache__/ and outputs/. PICTURE: Thursday's growth scare was not a one-day event. Over Friday the equity decline continued and broadened, credit widened 13bp to the month's wides, the 10Y stayed below 5.00 pct despite another 3 pct on Brent, and the dollar still would not bid. The two things that did NOT deteriorate are worth equal weight: rate vol retraced a third of its spike, and the consumer-sentiment tile turned out to be a board error rather than a collapse. Nothing in the hard data has broken - claims are at a three-month low, the LEI six-month rate is positive, financial conditions are still clearly looser than average, no Saudi barrel is offline and the central Iranian claim behind Friday's oil move is unverified and officially disputed. What has broken is the price of risk: credit at the month's wides, duration bid through an oil shock, breakevens 15bp below their band. That is a market that has stopped pricing an inflation shock and started pricing a growth and cost-of-capital shock, and it now goes into an FOMC. WATCH, IN ORDER OF WEIGHT: the Oct 23 T5YIFR print once FRED posts it, because a sustained sub-2.30 breakeven reframes this whole board from inflation risk to growth risk; the Oct 28 NFCI, the first read containing both risk-off sessions; whether HY OAS keeps widening past 340 or stabilises; the Oct 27-28 FOMC, where the risk has flipped dovish; whether the seven-tanker claim is ever verified and whether any Saudi barrel is actually confirmed offline; whether gold's break below 4,000 extends; rotating the embedded PAT.
